Estimated ingest volumes, implementation steps, hardware requirements, onboarding effort, and startup sequencing depend on the customer's actual environment, logging configuration, retention requirements, network design, app usage, and final architecture. Validate with customer-specific measurements and qualified Splunk/Cisco technical personnel before final purchase, deployment, or implementation commitments. This is not a quote, license commitment, capacity guarantee, or fixed professional services estimate.

cloud_uf_forwarding.label: Forward data to Splunk Cloud Platform (Universal Forwarder)

cloud_uf_credentials.label: Splunk Cloud Universal Forwarder credentials package

referenceHardware.summary: Use official Splunk reference hardware as a baseline. Actual hardware depends on ingest volume, search concurrency, retention, clustering, premium apps, and workload mix.
referenceHardware.minimumIndexer: Minimum indexer reference baseline includes 12 physical CPU cores or 24 vCPU, 12 GB RAM, storage sized for retention and I/O requirements, and a 1 Gb NIC.

universalForwarder.title: Universal Forwarder — high-level steps
steps: Download the Universal Forwarder from Splunk.
Install on the source host using the platform-appropriate installer.
Configure outputs.conf to forward to the Splunk destination (indexers, heavy forwarder, or Splunk Cloud receiving endpoint).
For Splunk Cloud, install and configure the Splunk Cloud Platform Universal Forwarder credentials package.
Configure inputs (monitored logs, Windows event channels, scripted inputs, or TA-driven modular inputs).
Restart the forwarder and validate connectivity.
Confirm events arrive in Splunk with expected sourcetype, host, and index.

cloud.label: Splunk Cloud Platform
cloud.overview: Splunk operates indexers and search heads. Customer teams focus on access, app/add-on installation, data onboarding, forwarder deployment, and validation.
approach: Confirm Splunk Cloud tenant access, roles, and onboarding contacts.
Install required apps and add-ons via Splunk Cloud vetting or approved private app process.
Define indexes, retention, and HEC tokens where applicable.
Deploy Universal Forwarders or approved collection methods (syslog via SC4S, HEC, vendor add-ons).
Install Splunk Cloud forwarder credentials on forwarders where required.
Validate data flow, field extraction, and dashboard readiness.
focusAreas: Required apps/add-ons and TA modular inputs
Universal Forwarder deployment and credentials package
caveats: Splunk Cloud limits certain inputs.conf configurations — use Data Manager and approved onboarding patterns.
Private apps require Splunk Cloud vetting before installation.
Hybrid paths need network and security review for forwarder-to-cloud connectivity.

onprem.label: Customer-managed Splunk Enterprise
onprem.overview: Customer provisions and operates Splunk Enterprise infrastructure including indexers, search heads, and forwarders.
approach: Confirm supported OS and Splunk Enterprise system requirements.
Plan deployment topology (standalone, distributed, indexer cluster, search head cluster).
Provision hosts using reference hardware as a baseline.
Install Splunk Enterprise on Linux or Windows per official documentation.
Configure indexes.conf, retention, and licensing.
Install required apps and technical add-ons.
Deploy Universal Forwarders, syslog collectors, or heavy forwarders as needed.
Validate ingest, search, and dashboard readiness.
focusAreas: System requirements and reference hardware sizing
Indexer and search head cluster design
caveats: Actual hardware and storage must be sized for ingest, retention, search load, and premium apps.
Clustering and multisite designs add operational complexity — validate with Splunk architecture guidance.
Change management and security hardening are customer responsibilities.

hybrid.label: Hybrid (Splunk Cloud + on-premises collection)
hybrid.overview: Combine Splunk Cloud for analytics with on-premises forwarders, syslog collectors, or heavy forwarders based on source location and network constraints.
approach: Identify which sources originate on-premises vs. cloud/SaaS.
Use Splunk Cloud onboarding patterns for cloud-native sources (HEC, vendor cloud add-ons).
Deploy on-premises forwarders or SC4S for datacenter and endpoint sources.
Validate network paths, latency, encryption, and firewall rules for forwarder-to-cloud traffic.
Install Splunk Cloud forwarder credentials where forwarders send to Splunk Cloud.
Align index routing and retention across hybrid boundaries.
Validate end-to-end search and correlation across onboarded sources.
focusAreas: Source location and collection method per zone
Splunk Cloud forwarder credentials and outputs configuration
SC4S or heavy forwarder tiers in DMZ or collector zones
Security and change-control for hybrid data paths
caveats: Hybrid design requires validation of source location, network path, latency, and security constraints.
Duplicate collection paths can inflate ingest — coordinate firewall, proxy, and SASE overlap.
Not every on-premises input pattern is supported directly in Splunk Cloud — use approved forwarding tiers.

collectionMethodExamples: Universal Forwarder — endpoint and server log collection
Syslog / Splunk Connect for Syslog (SC4S) — network and security appliances
HTTP Event Collector (HEC) — cloud APIs and application telemetry
API / modular input — vendor add-ons and SaaS integrations
Heavy Forwarder — intermediate parsing and routing tier
